title: One client project, 16 weeks
content_html:
See how undated pages move from the overall goal to daily work. ﻿͏  ﻿͏  ﻿͏  ﻿͏  ﻿͏  ﻿͏  ﻿͏  ﻿͏
 
Papier

Project planning

Give one client project a place on paper

Hi there,

For a substantial client project, a defined paper planning cycle can make the full stretch of work easier to see—without tying it to fixed calendar dates.

Papier’s Your Plans on Paper is a softback spiral productivity planner with 16 weeks of undated pages. It combines clear goal breakdowns with monthly, weekly and daily planning, giving the overall goal and the work beneath it one bounded place on paper.

Because the pages are undated, the planning cycle can begin when the project does. The structure stays specific: one 16-week span, viewed from the monthly picture down to the day’s work.

The product page lets you flick through the planner and inspect those monthly, weekly and daily pages. See whether the structure fits the way you want to organise one client project.

 
Look inside the planner

- Papier

asset_metadata.single_idea: Give one client project a defined 16-week place on paper, moving from goal breakdowns to monthly, weekly and daily planning.

selected_brief.selection_reason: The reader has a bounded 16-week job, and the strongest licensed evidence describes an undated 16-week planner with goal breakdowns and planning pages at three time scales. This gives a product-aware prospect something concrete to inspect without assuming their current tools or failures.

value_case.reader_benefit: For a suitable client project, the freelancer can place the overall goal and its monthly, weekly and daily work within one bounded paper planning cycle.
decision_conditions: The planning cycle covers 16 weeks and uses undated pages.
The evidence establishes monthly, weekly and daily pages, not a continuous rolling-date view or links to digital notes.

selected_brief.target_audience: A goal-driven professional starting a focused 16-week push and wanting planning away from screens
selected_brief.job: Get the reader to inspect the planner and decide whether its 16-week paper structure fits one substantial client project.
selected_brief.single_idea: Give one client project a defined 16-week place on paper, moving from goal breakdowns to monthly, weekly and daily planning.
selected_brief.mechanism: The productivity planner provides 16 weeks of undated pages, supported by goal breakdowns and pages for monthly, weekly and daily planning.

alternative_arguments.selection_reason: This is a distinct supported bet for a freelancer who cares less about planning at several time scales and more about maintaining visibility on progress throughout a client project.

value_case.reader_benefit: For a suitable client project, the freelancer can use documented accountability tools and reflection prompts to record progress during the planning cycle.
decision_conditions: The available evidence does not describe the individual accountability tools or the frequency and structure of the reflections.

alternative_arguments.single_idea: A focused client project can have a paper record of both planned work and progress, using accountability tracking tools and reflections.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: Papier's productivity planners include accountability tracking tools and reflections for tracking progress.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: a paper planner may appear useful only for writing down tasks. After: this planner also provides documented ways to record accountability and reflect on progress during a client project.
must_not_say: Do not claim the planner guarantees accountability, consistent use, project completion or improved performance.
Do not describe the individual accountability tools or reflection cadence; the evidence does not specify them.
Do not claim time savings or comparative superiority.
alternative_arguments.objection: The reader may wonder whether the planner supports reviewing progress rather than merely recording tasks.
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether documented accountability and reflection features are relevant to how the reader wants to manage a client project.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: The productivity-planner page describes the available accountability tracking tools and progress reflections at the level documented by Papier.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: The page evidence does not establish the tools' detailed format, their frequency or any resulting improvement in project delivery.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Present progress review as the practical reason to consider paper planning, anchored to a focused client project without promising an outcome.

selected_brief.belief_shift: Before: a paper planner may feel too general for a substantial client project. After: the reader can see a specific 16-week structure spanning the goal and its monthly, weekly and daily work, and can inspect whether that structure fits.
must_not_say: Do not claim a continuous current-day-centred view or any mechanism linking notes with dates or follow-ups.
Do not imply that Papier replaces, integrates with or synchronises with Obsidian, Microsoft 365, NotePlan or another digital tool.
Do not state or imply that the recipient currently uses any named tool, has failed with a previous system or has experienced the researched problem.
Do not promise that the planner will ensure goal achievement, project completion, faster delivery, better focus or improved performance.
Do not generalise the fit beyond freelancers delivering a client project.
Do not invoke customer adoption, testimonials, social proof or competitor superiority.
Do not add unverified pricing, delivery terms, guarantees, page counts or layout details.
Do not turn the email into a catalogue of unrelated Papier products, sustainability claims, packaging details or wedding features.
The planner documents monthly, weekly and daily planning pages, but not a rolling current-day-centered calendar or links between notes and dates.
selected_brief.objection: Will an undated paper planner provide enough structure for a substantial project without forcing it into fixed calendar dates?
selected_brief.tone: Warm, polished and quietly practical, with Papier's light playfulness kept secondary to the concrete planning mechanism.
selected_brief.next_step_decision: Decide whether the planner's 16-week structure and monthly, weekly and daily pages fit the way the reader wants to organise one client project.
selected_brief.next_step_value: The product page lets the reader look inside the Your Plans on Paper planner and inspect the documented monthly, weekly and daily planning structure.
selected_brief.next_step_limit: Looking inside does not establish a continuous rolling-date overview, links between notes and follow-up dates, compatibility with digital tools or a guaranteed project outcome.
selected_brief.subject_strategy: Make the bounded 16-week client project the reason to open, with paper as the concrete format; avoid generic productivity promises and unsupported claims about the reader's current workflow.
